TWO WAYS A SUITE ADVERTISES PROTECTION IT DOES NOT PROVIDE. Test and harness files only; no source file is in this ticket's change, and that is asserted structurally in section 13 of THE-352.suite-guards.test.ts rather than read off the diff (#454, #482).

PART 1 - THE EXACT TRIGGER. Four suites (THE-286.settings-chrome-autosave, THE-296.settings-sections, THE-300.billing-surface, AdminSettings.regroup) shared an inherited three-regex code() helper. Its JSX-comment rule, /\{\s*\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/\s*\}/, is broken by an ORDINARY OPENING BRACE FOLLOWED BY A DOCBLOCK - not by an unterminated construct, a // inside a string, or a URL. `interface IntegrationsSectionProps {` is followed by a JSDoc on its first member, so the pattern anchors there; the quantifier is lazy, but laziness stops only at the first */ that is ALSO followed by \s*}, and nothing in the file closes that way until `catch { /* prefill is a convenience, not a requirement */ }` 154 lines later - lines 34 to 187, 85 of them code. The props interface, the component signature, isPlatformOverride, the per-provider gate, the provider state and the whole loader became one space. MEASURED, NOT ARGUED: three defects planted inside that span - a text-red-600 palette class, a mail.google.com scope and a $49/mo price literal - were run against the four suites at origin/main and all 152 tests passed; the same plants against the repaired suites fail five named assertions. Swept across every tracked .ts/.tsx in src/, the old helper loses code the parser keeps in EIGHTY-NINE files; only IntegrationsSection.tsx is one the four suites read, but the rest are a standing trap for any guard that adopts the helper, which is how it reached four suites. The replacement is THE-346's parser-driven stripper, IMPORTED not copied: it was written as a shared module on purpose, nine suites already import it, and importing adds a line to this ticket's own files while editing nothing shared - so it serialises no other PR, which copying a third time would eventually force.

PART 2 - THE HANG IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE AND THIS TICKET DOES NOT CHASE IT. Seven tickets failed to reproduce #477's three dead suites; THE-349 showed the '~3 hour hang' was a stale GitHub jobs API reading; this ticket's baseline at 6b11c014e is 480 files / 13,184 passing with ZERO skipped; and all three named suites (THE-279.toolbar-layout, THE-286.settings-chrome-autosave.layout, THE-296.settings-sections.layout) already carry the @vitest-environment node pragma THE-338 identified, so that is not the missing cause either. THE REPORTING DEFECT IS REAL REGARDLESS and is the deliverable. VITEST CANNOT BE CONFIGURED OUT OF IT - measured on 4.1.9: a beforeAll that throws fails the SUITE and its children are never started, so they report skipped, while a beforeEach that throws fails each test. There is no option that moves one into the other. So setUpOrFail (src/test/support/suite-setup.ts) runs the caller's body in beforeAll with the caller's own timeout, CATCHES its failure and rethrows it from beforeEach. Applied to 37 of the 39 suites that open a measuring browser, not only the three named: the rest carry the identical defect. TWO ARE LEFT UNCONVERTED AND BYTE-IDENTICAL TO main, named in UNCONVERTED in THE-352.suite-guards.test.ts, because converting either means editing a pin this repo forbids editing. THE-308.month-view.layout.test.tsx is pinned by a bare expect(sha(...)).toBe(...) in THE-351's inbox layout suite with no register beside it, and the house rule is APPENDED NEVER SUBSTITUTED - main went red for everyone the week a PR replaced a pinned digest - so there is nothing to append to and giving that pin an append path is a ticket of its own. THE-305.course-editor-header.layout.test.tsx is pinned by THE-311's section 8, which reads git diff --name-only against the base ref and asserts the file is absent from it: that is a guard about the CURRENT BRANCH'S DIFF, the shape #454 sweeps for and #482 found inside THE-315's own section 2, and its premise ('THE-311 did not touch this') expired when THE-311 landed in #447, so it now fires for any later branch that touches the file. THE-311 already retired one assertion of exactly that shape in the same file for exactly that reason; this one was missed. REPORTED, NOT REPAIRED - loosening another ticket's guard is not this ticket's call - and the two suites are left untouched rather than half-edited, which a guard here asserts. Verified end to end - the same planted setup failure in THE-296's layout suite reports 17 SKIPPED at origin/main and 17 FAILED here.

THE HARNESS. browser-measure.ts now disposes what it spawns: open() kills and reaps its browser on any failure path between the spawn and the first settled page; send() is bounded at 60s, which is a NEW bound where there was none rather than a loosened one, so an unanswered CDP request - THE-333 traced the original stall to the WebSocket connect or to settle(), which awaits a requestAnimationFrame a headless Chrome can decline to fire - fails diagnosably instead of waiting forever; and a browser still live when the worker is terminated is SIGKILLed on the way out. The sweep listens for SIGTERM as well as exit because exit alone does not fire on the path that leaks - Vitest terminates a worker by signal and registers no handler itself - and it uses once plus a re-raise so Node's default termination, and therefore the worker's exit code, is unchanged. THE-333's PID-derived-port collision was already fixed and is pinned here, not re-fixed.

WHAT IS NOT PINNED ABOVE, AND WHY. This ticket edits 41 suites belonging to other tickets - the four whose stripper it replaces and the 37 it converts to setUpOrFail - and CANNOT record a digest for any of them: THE-340 found that THE-322's index guard reads a ticket name in a structural field as a record listing another record, so a ticket editing another ticket's suite has to say so in prose, as THE-340 did. The edits are uniform and mechanical: in the four, one helper definition plus one import line; in the 37, `beforeAll(` becomes `setUpOrFail(` at the file's single top-level setup hook, one import is added and the now-unused beforeAll leaves the vitest import. Not one assertion was added, removed, reordered, retired or loosened in any of them, and no timeout was changed. AdminSettings.regroup.test.tsx is additionally recorded in settings-freeze-register.ts, which is the append path its pin provides. NO firestore.rules DIGEST IS RECORDED HERE, deliberately: THE-333 and THE-341 both recorded one and both turned THE-325 red. firestore.indexes.json, functions/ and every file under src/app, src/lib and src/components are untouched.

entries.why: THE-352 leaves the measuring harness here. Three changes, all about a browser outliving the thing that opened it, and none of them touches what the harness MEASURES. (1) open() disposes in its own catch: everything between the spawn and the first settled page is wrapped, and on any failure the browser is killed and reaped before the error is rethrown. It used to depend entirely on the caller having assigned its `browser` variable before awaiting so that afterAll had something to close - a convention every suite happens to keep, and no guarantee. (2) send() is bounded at 60s. It previously resolved only on a matching reply and had no reject path at all, so a browser that died mid-request, or a Runtime.evaluate whose awaited promise never settled, left the caller waiting forever; settle() awaits requestAnimationFrame, which a headless Chrome can decline to fire, and THE-333 traced the original stall to exactly there. This is a NEW bound, not a loosened one - 60s is far longer than any real CDP round trip and far shorter than any suite timeout, so the failure lands inside the hook that caused it and names the method. (3) Every live browser is registered and SIGKILLed on the way out, for THE-333's twenty leaked Chromiums: each leak holds memory on a two-core runner and makes the next launch likelier to fail, which is intermittency with a cause. The sweep listens for SIGTERM as well as exit - measured: Vitest terminates a worker by signal and registers no handler of its own, so with exit alone nothing runs on the path that leaks - and uses `once` plus a re-raise to self, so the listener removes itself and the worker then dies exactly as it would have, one sweep later. The error messages, the stderr capture, the kernel-assigned --remote-debugging-port=0 and close()'s awaited teardown are unchanged.

NEW, and the deliverable of Part 2. setUpOrFail runs a suite's setup body in beforeAll with the caller's own timeout forwarded verbatim, catches whatever it throws, and rethrows it from a beforeEach. Vitest fails an individual test when beforeEach throws and skips it when beforeAll does, so this is what turns #477's 61 silently absent assertions into 61 reported failures. It cannot be done by configuration: measured on vitest 4.1.9, a suite-hook failure is a suite error whose children are never started, and no option moves them. The helper swallows nothing - on success it is inert, on failure the error surfaces once per test carrying its original stack - and it deliberately does NOT let the tests run against a half-built fixture, which would be worse than the skip because the assertions would then measure an unopened browser. AND IT ENFORCES THE CALLER'S BUDGET ITSELF, which is the half that matters for #477: nothing threw there, three suites simply sat in beforeAll until the hook ran out of time, and a hook aborted at its timeout is aborted by the RUNNER from outside the callback - so catching around the body would have missed the reported failure mode entirely and left the tests skipped. The body is raced against the caller's timeoutMs and the HOOK is given a fixed 5s tie-break on top, so the body's own deadline is the one that fires and lands inside the catch. That is not a loosened timeout: the body still gets exactly what the caller asked for, a suite that passed 180_000 still fails at 180_000, and the grace is a constant rather than a proportion precisely so a slow suite gains no real extra time. Verified on a real measuring suite: a hanging setup in THE-296's layout suite reports 17 skipped without this and 17 failed with it, each naming the budget it missed.

NEW - this ticket's own guards, and every claim in them that can be checked by breaking something is checked that way, because reading is what missed fourteen defective guards in this series. The stripper is fed a defect planted in the previously-eaten span and must see it, with the mirror case asserting the shipped file is clean so the pattern is not trivially true. The hook helper is run as a CHILD vitest process against two probe suites - a bare beforeAll and a setUpOrFail failing identically - and its JSON report is read, because a suite cannot observe its own tests being skipped. The harness is given a stand-in browser through CHROME_PATH and its pid is looked for afterwards, on the failure path and on the abandoned path. Every one of those was mutation-verified: reverting the stripper, reverting one suite to a bare beforeAll, removing open()'s catch, removing the signal sweep and removing the CDP bound each turn the matching guard red. Sections 10 to 13 are the house rules over this PR's own files - no line number pinned, no date literal, nothing that reads the branch's diff, nothing but test and harness paths, LF only - and the branch-reference patterns there are composed from fragments rather than spelt, because a guard that writes origin/main inside itself matches itself and gets deleted rather than kept.
